# Delegation grants

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P4 · Agents everywhere](../README.md#phase-4--agents-everywhere) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:delegation-grants` · **Epic:** [#166](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/166) · **Tickets:** 12 (3S 9M)

Users approve delegation grants that let one registered agent act for them, for a stated purpose, with a fixed tool set, a fixed set of per-user providers and an expiry. The token service mints grant-bound tokens carrying `grant_id`, `tools` and `providers`, and the worker only narrows: MCP tools/call outside the grant is denied and per-user secrets are swapped only for listed providers. A revoke is refused by the token service at once, denied fleet-wide within one bundle long-poll (open sessions are closed), and lasts at most one token TTL while the CP is down. The guarantee holds for agents in identity require mode with `delegation: required`; the feature is off unless the CP-local `grants.enabled` is set.

## How we build it

- Gate and config: a CP-local `grants:` block (new internal/config/grants.go, `json:"-"`, read only from the operator --config like `tokenService:`). Keys: enabled (default false), maxTTL (default 168h, hard cap 2160h; also the TTL used when the agent omits expires_in), pendingTTL (24h), maxTools (default 32, hard cap 64), maxPendingPerUserAgent (3), maxPendingPerUser (20), maxActivePerUserAgent (20), rateLimit {perAgent, perUser} for grant creation in the `policy.ParseRateLimit` grammar, sweepInterval (1m), expiryNoticeBefore (72h), noticeInterval (1h) and `agents: {<id>: {maxTTL}}` (each at most the 2160h hard cap). Purpose is 1-200 runes. Startup fails unless tokenService.enabled, consent is configured, `--bundles=offer|require` and `--state-dir` are all set, with an error naming the missing piece. When disabled: every grants route returns 404, no grants tables are created, no `revokedGrants` section is served and /policy stays byte-identical.
- Data model: new package internal/grants on cpstate, migration `grants/0001`. Table `grants` (named apart from the P3 `oauth_grants` table and the portal 'connections' routes): id (`grt_` + 128-bit crypto/rand base64url); identity snapshot idp_iss, sub, email, email_verified, groups_json (capped at 64), captured from the verified ID token at request time and refreshed from the approving portal.Principal; agent_id; purpose (agent-supplied, 1-200 runes, no control or bidi characters, stored and shown as untrusted text); requested_tools_json, tools_json (approved), requested_providers_json, providers_json; requested_expires_at, expires_at, pending_expires_at; status pending|active|denied|revoked|expired; revision, created_at, decided_at, revoked_at, revoked_by_kind (user|admin|agent|offboard|system), revoked_by, revoke_reason (closed set), renewed_from, expiry_notified_at. Indexes (idp_iss, sub, status), (agent_id, status), (status, expires_at). Rows are never deleted. Table `grant_events` holds agent and system transitions (see Recording). The `grants.Store` interface ships with a `grantstest.Run` conformance suite for p5-postgres-ha.
- Lifecycle: one transition function is the only status writer, using UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status=? AND revision=?. Allowed: pending->active (approve), pending->denied, pending->expired (pendingTTL), pending->revoked (agent cancel, admin, offboarding), active->revoked, active->expired. Anything else is ErrInvalidTransition; a lost race is ErrConflict. Narrowing happens only at approval (tools and providers are a subset of the request, expiry no later than requested). Active grants are never narrowed in P4; the user revokes and the agent requests again.
- Tool identifiers: a grant lists tools exactly as the gateway's ToolPolicy sees them, grammar `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}(__[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64})?$`, deduped and sorted, at most maxTools entries, which keeps a grant token under the P2 12 KiB cap. A bare `tool` matches that tool on any server. A `server__tool` entry matches only when the worker knows the server id for the request (the p4-mcp-registry host mapping or the P4 MCP hub); otherwise it matches nothing (fail closed). No wildcards.
- Agent API, mounted under `/oauth2/grants*` beside `/oauth2/token` because both use the same client-assertion auth (never under `/dashboard/api/*`, which is session/API-key authenticated, or `/api/`, which is reserved for a future public API), all authenticated by the agent's private_key_jwt through `tokensvc.VerifyClientAssertion` and the ReplayStore (each call needs a fresh jti), with form bodies only, the TOKX-04 per-IP and per-agent limiters, and authz rows classified assertion-authenticated, ScopeNone, Audited:false. `POST /oauth2/grants` {subject_token (user ID token), purpose, tools, providers, expires_in} verifies the subject with the P2 OIDC verifier and allowedAZP, the BlockChecker and the agent's allowed_groups; tools must be in the served settings mcp.tools allow list minus deny (and in registry approvedTools when the registry is configured); providers must be configured consent providers; expiry (default 168h when expires_in is omitted) is clamped to maxTTL or the per-agent maxTTL. Responses: 201 {grant_id, status, approve_url, status_url, expires_at, expires_in_clamped, pending_expires_at}; 400 tools_not_allowed or providers_not_allowed naming only the offending entries; 401 invalid_client; 400 invalid_grant/subject_*; 429 too_many_pending or rate_limited; 503 temporarily_unavailable/idp_unavailable. Also `POST /oauth2/grants/{id}/status` (long-poll), `POST /oauth2/grants/{id}/renew` and `POST /oauth2/grants/{id}/cancel`. Another agent's or an unknown grant gets the same 404 body.
- Consent: `/portal/grants` and `/portal/grants/{id}` behind the W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session; decisions are `POST /portal/api/grants/{id}/approve` {tools, providers, expires_at, revision} and `/deny`, sent through the portal api() wrapper with X-Warden-CSRF and the Origin check. Only the session whose (iss, sub) equals the grant sees it; anyone else gets the byte-identical 404 body. The page shows Warden-built facts first (registry display name and owner, tools grouped by server, providers, expiry from the CP clock, 'Signed in as'), then the purpose with textContent under the fixed label 'Purpose stated by the agent (not verified)', and a notice when the agent's delegation mode is optional. The server intersects the posted sets with the request and with currently allowed tools, rejects a stale revision or non-pending grant with 409, and re-checks the block list and agent status.
- Token service: a `SubjectResolver` registered in tokensvc for `urn:warden:params:token-type:grant` (W-P2-TOKX-02 dispatch map; Exchange is not rewritten). subject_token is the grant id, which is not a credential because the assertion's agent must equal grant.agent_id; unknown and mismatched ids give the same external error. The resolver reads the store on every exchange (no cache) and returns the snapshot subject; the common P2 steps then run (agent active, BlockChecker, groups snapshot against current allowed_groups, scope, SessionStore.Touch for sid so session revoke and offboarding apply, cnf.jkt from the assertion key). A user whose idp_links row is offboarded is refused. The token has header typ `wgt+jwt` (pre-grant workers require `wt+jwt` and reject it as malformed), claims grant_id, tools and providers, and exp = min(iat+ttl, grant expires_at). New reasons grant_not_found, grant_pending, grant_denied, grant_revoked, grant_expired, grant_agent_mismatch, grant_required, grant_unenforceable and grant_store_unavailable join the closed Reason enum; token_events gains grant_id.
- Delegation mode: an admin-only per-agent setting `agents[].delegation: optional|required` (default optional) served in SettingsWire next to `agents[].identity`. When required, the token service refuses id_token exchange for that agent with invalid_grant/grant_required, and the worker denies MCP tools/call from that agent's Warden tokens without grant_id with `mcp_grant_required`. Optional mode is documented as user-visible consent with no enforcement guarantee, because the agent can still exchange an ID token for an ungranted token. Without identity require mode an agent can omit its token, so the guarantee needs both require and delegation required.
- Worker enforcement: the WardenVerifier accepts typ `wgt+jwt` and parses grant_id, tools and providers into identity.Claims once per verify (cached in the P2 (generation, sha256) LRU); SubjectFrom fills Subject.GrantID, GrantTools and GrantProviders. The gateway reads them from the W-P1-GPOL-04 `gateway.RequestMeta{Subject}`, so no second seam is added; http.go mcpRequestScan and the ws pump already pass the verified subject, and stdio carries no token (documented). When GrantID is set: the grant check runs after policy, AllowWhen and task scope (policy reasons stay dominant; the grant only narrows). Known behaviour, accepted for P4: because ToolPolicy.Evaluate runs first, an out-of-grant call that policy allows still consumes one tool rate-limit token before it is denied; there is no non-consuming evaluate in P4 and denies an out-of-grant tool with `mcp_grant_scope` whatever `mcp.mode` says; an unparseable or batch body is denied with `mcp_grant_unparsed` whatever FailClosedOnError says; a worker whose MCP gateway is nil or disabled refuses grant tokens with 403 `grant_unenforceable`. Per-user swaps through the W-P3-PUS-09 UserTokenSource happen under a grant token only for providers in the claim; any other provider gets 403 `grant_provider_scope` and no swap.
- Rollout safety: workers that implement grants add heartbeat cap `grants/v1`. Following the W-P2-WBND-07 pattern, the token service refuses grant exchange with temporarily_unavailable/grant_unenforceable while a connected worker reporting that agent lacks the cap (admin `force` override recorded in admin audit). Together with the new typ, no mixed-version fleet can treat a grant token as unrestricted.
- Revocation: the owner uses `POST /portal/api/grants/{id}/revoke`; admins use `POST /dashboard/api/grants/{id}/revoke` and `POST /dashboard/api/grants/revoke` {sub|agent} (admin role, Audited true, Scope `grants:write`); the agent uses `/oauth2/grants/{id}/cancel`. Offboarding appends a `revoke_delegation_grants` Step to the W-P3-OFFB-01 contain stage through a narrow GrantRevoker interface. The token service refuses at once. A named signed-bundle section `revokedGrants: [{id, until}]` (until = revoked_at + tokenService.ttl + identity clockSkewSeconds) is built from the store on every Refresh (so it survives a CP restart), with publish_log reason `grant_revoked`, publishes coalesced within 1s, entries pruned after until, a hard cap of 10,000 entries (above it the CP keeps the previous envelope, logs at error and raises a Finding) and no key when empty. Workers check the revoked set on every verify and every terminated MCP request, and after each apply close registered sessions whose grant_id was just revoked through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 registry and the W-P2-WBND-09 post-apply re-check. Grant expiry needs no list because token exp never exceeds it.
- Recording: user and admin decisions (approve with the narrowed diff, deny, revoke) go through adminaudit.Recorder with auth_method portal or session/apikey. Agent and system transitions (request, renew, cancel, expire, offboard revoke) go to the cpstate `grant_events` table plus one `warden.grant.v1` slog line, keeping machine events out of the hash-chained admin audit as P2 decided for token_events. analytics.Event gains GrantID (json `grant_id`, omitempty), added to warden.decision.v1 with a schema_rev bump and to the FleetSQLiteStore; `grant_id` in tokens and decision lines always means a `grt_` delegation grant, never a P3 oauth_grants id. CP counters warden_cp_grants_transitions_total{to} and gauge warden_cp_grants{status}; worker deny reasons on the existing blocked counter. No sub, grant id or tool labels; no tokens, assertions or purpose text in logs.
- Notifications: internal/grants defines a nil-safe Notifier seam so the request path compiles without p4-notify. W-P4-DGR-09 wires it to internal/notify: `grant_approval` on create, `grant_expiring` once per grant before expiry, `grant_blocked` on a revoked or expired exchange (at most one per grant per 24h, pre-filtered in a cpstate table and deduped again by the notify family window); every send uses Ref `grant:<id>`. Payloads hold only the registry display name, a grant id prefix, counts, expires_at and a portal link; never tokens, assertions or purpose text. Without notify configured the sends are no-ops; the agent shows approve_url itself.
- Degraded modes: IdP down gives 503 idp_unavailable on POST /oauth2/grants, while exchanges for approved grants keep working (no IdP call) and approval works for existing portal sessions. CP down: no new grants or tokens; live grant tokens work until exp (at most one TTL) and revocation waits for the CP. The CP clock is authoritative for grant expiry; workers apply identity clockSkewSeconds. A restart loses nothing because all state is in cpstate and status waiters re-read. Long-poll waiters and the sweepers are single-replica until p5-postgres-ha. After a backup restore (W-P1-OPS1-04) an admin re-applies revocations with the bulk revoke route; this is in the runbook.

## Done when

On a deployment with tokenService, consent, `--bundles=require` and `grants.enabled` set, and an agent in identity require mode with `delegation: required`: the agent gets a Warden token only through a grant the user approved (and could narrow) in the portal, and an id_token exchange for it is refused with grant_required; the worker denies MCP tools/call outside the grant with mcp_grant_scope over HTTP and WebSocket, in monitor mode and for malformed or batch bodies, and swaps per-user credentials only for granted providers; a worker without `grants/v1` never honours a grant token; after a user or admin revoke or an offboarding the token service refuses the next exchange at once and every pinned worker denies the live token and closes its open sessions within one bundle long-poll; user and admin decisions appear once in the admin audit and agent or system transitions once in grant_events; decision lines carry grant_id; and all of this survives a CP restart.

### 1/12 · W-P4-DGR-01

**Add grants config, model, SQLite store and transitions**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#167](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/167)

Create the CP library the rest of the feature builds on: the CP-local `grants:` config block, new package internal/grants with the Grant model, the identity snapshot, a single transition function and a SQLite store on cpstate. It also defines the Recorder and Notifier seams so later tickets write audit and notification calls without importing each other. Nothing calls it yet and the block defaults to off, so merging changes no behaviour.

**Requirements**

- New internal/config/grants.go: GrantsConfig{Enabled, MaxTTL, PendingTTL, MaxTools, MaxPendingPerUserAgent, MaxPendingPerUser, MaxActivePerUserAgent, RateLimit{PerAgent, PerUser}, SweepInterval, ExpiryNoticeBefore, NoticeInterval, Agents map[string]{MaxTTL}} with `json:"-"`, defaults (enabled false, MaxTTL 168h, PendingTTL 24h, MaxTools 32, 3, 20, 20, 1m, 72h, 1h), hard caps (MaxTTL and every Agents[id].MaxTTL 2160h, MaxTools 64; a larger value fails config load naming the field) and config.LoadGrants(path) on the LoadTokenService pattern; the block never reaches SettingsWire.
- New internal/grants: Grant with the design fields (idp_iss, sub, email, email_verified, groups, agent_id, purpose, requested and approved tools and providers, requested_expires_at, expires_at, pending_expires_at, status, revision, decided_at, revoked_at, revoked_by_kind, revoked_by, revoke_reason, renewed_from, expiry_notified_at), the closed Status and RevokedByKind sets, and NewID() returning `grt_` + 128-bit crypto/rand base64url.
- Validation: purpose 1-200 runes with no control or bidi characters; tools match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}(__[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64})?$`, deduped, sorted, 1..MaxTools; providers are known provider ids; groups capped at 64. Errors name the field, never the value.
- cpstate migration `grants/0001` creates `grants` (indexes (idp_iss, sub, status), (agent_id, status), (status, expires_at)) and `grant_events(id, ts, grant_id, kind, actor_kind, actor, status_from, status_to, details_json)`; it runs only when grants.enabled is true. No column holds a token or assertion.
- One Transition writer: pending->active|denied|expired|revoked and active->revoked|expired, each a single UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status=? AND revision=?; anything else is ErrInvalidTransition and RowsAffected=0 is ErrConflict. Approve(id, tools, providers, expiresAt, revision, snapshot) returns ErrWidening for any entry not requested or an expiry later than requested.
- Store interface: Create, Get, ListBySub(iss, sub), ListByAgent, List(filter, cursor, limit<=200), Approve, Deny, Revoke(id, by, reason), RevokeAllForUser(iss, sub, by), ExpireDue(now) (active past expires_at and pending past pending_expires_at), MarkExpiryNotified, CountOpen(iss, sub, agent) and Subscribe(id) <-chan struct{} closed on every transition; plus grantstest.Run(t, Store) for the P5 Postgres store.
- Seams: grants.Recorder (admin decisions go to adminaudit.Recorder, agent and system events to grant_events plus one `warden.grant.v1` slog line) and a nil-safe grants.Notifier{Send(ctx, kind, iss, sub, data)}. The adminaudit closed details allowlist gains grant_id, agent_id, tools_count, tools_removed (capped at 64), providers_removed, expiry_shortened, status_from, status_to and reason_class.
- Logs carry only an 8-character grant id prefix and status; never email, purpose or groups.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/config/grants.go with GrantsConfig, defaults, validation and LoadGrants; extend rawConfig; add TestGrantsNotOnWire and TestWritersPreserveGrantsBlock next to the tokenService tests.
2. New internal/grants/grant.go: Grant, Status, RevokedByKind, NewID, ValidatePurpose, ValidateTools, ValidateProviders.
3. New internal/grants/transition.go: the allowed-transition table and Transition(from, to) error.
4. New internal/grants/store.go and store_sqlite.go: Store interface and SQLite implementation with cpstate migration `grants/0001`, registered with cpstate.Open only when enabled; Subscribe uses a per-id channel map closed on each committed transition.
5. New internal/grants/record.go: Recorder over adminaudit.Recorder and the grant_events table; add the grant details keys to the adminaudit allowlist; define the Notifier interface (nil-safe).
6. New internal/grants/grantstest/run.go: Run(t, Store) conformance suite; internal/grants/store_sqlite_test.go runs it.
7. Tests: TestTransitions (full from/to table), TestConcurrentTransitions (-race), TestApproveRejectsWidening, TestExpireDue with a fake clock, TestSubscribeWakesOnTransition, TestValidateTools.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given each (from, to) pair outside the allowed table, Transition returns ErrInvalidTransition and the row is unchanged: `go test ./internal/grants -run TestTransitions`.
- [ ] Given 20 goroutines racing Approve and Revoke on one pending grant, exactly one succeeds and the rest get ErrConflict or ErrInvalidTransition: `go test -race ./internal/grants -run TestConcurrentTransitions`.
- [ ] Given a request for tools [a,b] expiring in 7d, Approve with [a,c] or with 8d returns ErrWidening; Approve with [a] and 1d stores exactly [a] and the 1d expiry.
- [ ] Given an active grant 1s past expires_at and a pending grant past pending_expires_at on a fake clock, ExpireDue marks both expired and leaves an unexpired grant untouched.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/grants/... -run TestConformance` passes against the SQLite store, and with grants.enabled=false no grants tables exist in a fresh state dir.
- [ ] Given an empty `grants:` block, LoadGrants returns MaxTTL 168h, PendingTTL 24h and MaxTools 32; maxTTL 2161h, an agents[id].maxTTL of 2161h or maxTools 65 fails config load naming the field: `go test ./internal/config -run TestGrantsConfigDefaults`.

### 2/12 · W-P4-DGR-02

**Add the agent grant request API**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#168](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/168)

Add `POST /oauth2/grants` so an agent holding a user's ID token can ask that user for a narrow, time-limited grant. The agent and user are verified exactly as on /oauth2/token, the requested tools and providers are checked against what policy and consent already allow, and the expiry is clamped. The response gives the agent an approve_url to show the user and a status_url to poll. CP-only and mounted only when grants are enabled.

**Requirements**

- `POST /oauth2/grants` takes application/x-www-form-urlencoded (MaxBytesReader 32 KiB): client_assertion_type, client_assertion, subject_token, subject_token_type (id_token only), purpose, tools (repeated), providers (repeated, optional) and expires_in (optional; omitted means the effective maxTTL, 168h by default). JSON bodies, query-string assertions and Authorization headers give 400 invalid_request.
- The agent is authenticated with tokensvc.VerifyClientAssertion and the ReplayStore (W-P2-TOKX-01); the subject is verified with the same verifier, AllowedAZP, BlockChecker and allowed_groups check as W-P2-TOKX-02, and the agent must be active.
- Tools must be in the served settings mcp.tools allow list and not in deny (MCPToolsSettings); when the MCP registry is configured they must also be in the current approvedTools. Providers must be configured consent providers. Otherwise 400 {"error":"tools_not_allowed"|"providers_not_allowed", "names":[...]} listing only the offending entries; this check is advisory and the worker intersection stays authoritative.
- Expiry is clamped to grants.agents[id].maxTTL or grants.maxTTL and reported as expires_in_clamped; pending_expires_at = now + pendingTTL. maxPendingPerUserAgent, maxPendingPerUser and maxActivePerUserAgent give 429 too_many_pending; an identical open pending request (same agent, user, tools, providers) returns 200 with the existing grant instead of a new row.
- Response 201 {grant_id, status: pending, expires_at, expires_in_clamped, pending_expires_at, approve_url, status_url} with Cache-Control: no-store. approve_url is consent.publicURL (W-P3-JIT-01) + /portal/grants/<id>, the same page W-P4-NTFY-04 links for grant kinds, built only from CP config. Errors: 401 invalid_client, 400 invalid_grant/subject_invalid|subject_expired|user_blocked, 403 group_not_allowed, 429 rate_limited with Retry-After, 503 temporarily_unavailable/idp_unavailable.
- Authz table rows (W-P1-SSO-05/W-P2-APIK-02) classify POST /oauth2/grants assertion-authenticated, ScopeNone, Audited:false; console cookies, wwt_ and wak_ bearers are rejected. The TOKX-04 per-IP and per-agent limiters apply plus grants.rateLimit perAgent and perUser.
- Writes a grant_events `requested` row through grants.Recorder and calls the nil-safe grants.Notifier with grant_approval (a nil notifier or a send error never fails the request). Logs `msg=grant_requested agent grant_prefix tools_count clamped` with no subject token, assertion, email or purpose.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/grants/service.go: Service{Store, Recorder, Notifier, Config} with Request(ctx, agent, subject, req) doing validation, allowed-set checks, clamping, pending caps, dedupe and Create.
2. New internal/controlplane/grants_http.go: (s *Server) handleGrantCreate, mounted in Server.Handler only when Config.Grants (new *grants.Service) is non-nil, sharing the form parsing helpers of the /oauth2/token handler.
3. Wire the allowed-tool source from the served settings snapshot (internal/config/mcp.go MCPToolsSettings) and, when present, the registry approvedTools; wire providers from the consent provider list.
4. Add the authz table rows and extend TestAuthzRouteCoverage; reuse the tokensvc Limiter for the grant rate limits.
5. Tests in new internal/controlplane/grants_http_test.go: TestGrantRequestToolValidation, TestGrantRequestClampsTTL, TestGrantRequestAuth, TestGrantRequestPendingCaps, TestGrantRequestDedupe, TestGrantRoutesAbsentWhenDisabled, TestGrantRequestNoSecretsInLogs.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given tools [read_file, exec_cmd] where exec_cmd is in mcp.tools.deny, the response is 400 tools_not_allowed listing only exec_cmd and no row is created: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestGrantRequestToolValidation`.
- [ ] Given the default maxTTL 168h and expires_in of 60 days, 201 returns expires_at = now+168h and expires_in_clamped=true; with expires_in omitted expires_at = now+168h and expires_in_clamped=false; a per-agent maxTTL of 24h clamps to 24h instead: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestGrantRequestClampsTTL`.
- [ ] Given a forged assertion the response is 401 invalid_client; given a valid assertion with an expired subject or a blocked user it is 400 invalid_grant with the matching reason and no row: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestGrantRequestAuth`.
- [ ] Given 3 pending grants for one (user, agent), a 4th distinct request gets 429 too_many_pending, and a repeat of an existing request returns 200 with the same grant_id.
- [ ] With grants.enabled=false, POST /oauth2/grants returns 404 and `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRouteCoverage` passes with the new rows classified.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-01`](delegation-grants.md#112--w-p4-dgr-01) Add grants config, model, SQLite store and transitions; [`W-P2-TOKX-04`](token-exchange.md#47--w-p2-tokx-04) Add rate limits, issuance records and metrics for token exchange; [`W-P2-APIK-02`](api-keys.md#27--w-p2-apik-02) Authenticate API keys and enforce per-route scopes in the authz table; [`W-P2-AREG-01`](agent-registry.md#17--w-p2-areg-01) Add internal/agentreg store, schema and validation

### 3/12 · W-P4-DGR-03

**Build the grant approval pages in the consent portal**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#169](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/169)

Add the portal list and detail pages where the user approves, narrows or denies a pending grant. The page shows facts Warden built first and the agent's purpose only as clearly labelled, unverified text, following the W-P3-PORT-03 rule against consent phishing. Decisions go through the P3 `/portal/api/*` JSON convention with X-Warden-CSRF, and the server never lets a posted payload widen the request. CP-only.

**Requirements**

- Routes behind portal.RequireSession (W-P3-CSIG-04): GET /portal/grants, GET /portal/grants/{id}, GET /portal/api/grants, POST /portal/api/grants/{id}/approve {tools, providers, expires_at, revision} and POST /portal/api/grants/{id}/deny {revision}. Mutations need X-Warden-CSRF and the Origin check and use the W-P3-PORT-01 security headers and the per-session mutation limit.
- Only a session whose (iss, sub) equals the grant's (idp_iss, sub) can view or decide it; unknown ids and other users' ids return 404 with a byte-identical body containing no agent, tool or purpose string.
- The page shows the registry display name, owner and verified badge, tools grouped by server, providers, the requested expiry relative to the CP clock and 'Signed in as <email>' before the purpose; the purpose appears only under 'Purpose stated by the agent (not verified)', is set with textContent and is never linkified. A notice is shown when the agent's delegation mode is optional.
- Approve stores tools ∩ requested ∩ currently allowed tools, providers ∩ requested, and min(expires_at, requested_expires_at); an empty tool set gives 400 no_tools, a stale revision or non-pending grant gives 409. The block list and agent status are re-checked; a blocked user gets 403 user_blocked and an inactive agent 409 agent_disabled.
- On approve the identity snapshot (email, email_verified, groups capped at 64) is refreshed from portal.Principal. grant.approved (with tools_removed, providers_removed, expiry_shortened) and grant.denied are written to adminaudit with auth_method portal and actor user:<sub prefix>.
- Logs `msg=portal_grant_decision outcome grant_prefix tools_kept tools_removed` with no email or purpose. With consent or grants disabled every /portal/grants* and /portal/api/grants* path returns 404.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/portal/grants.go: list, detail and decision handlers behind portal.RequireSession, with the owner check via portal.PrincipalFrom and a shared notFound body.
2. grants.Service gains Approve(ctx, id, principal, decision) and Deny, which re-intersect with the current allowed tools and call Store.Approve or Deny with the revision.
3. New embedded internal/portal/static/grants.html and grants.js using the existing portal api() wrapper; all values rendered with textContent.
4. Wire the portal routes in internal/controlplane when Config.Grants is non-nil; add a Grants link to the portal nav without changing the connections API.
5. Tests in new internal/portal/grants_test.go: TestGrantDecisionNarrow, TestGrantDecisionNoWidening, TestGrantOtherUser404, TestGrantDecisionRequiresCSRF, TestGrantDecisionStaleRevision409, TestGrantPurposeRenderedAsText.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a pending grant for [a,b,c], when the owner approves [a,c] with a 1d expiry, the stored grant is active with tools [a,c] and expires_at now+1d: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestGrantDecisionNarrow`.
- [ ] Given an approve payload edited to [a,z] where z was never requested, or a later expiry, the stored grant holds only [a] and at most the requested expiry: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestGrantDecisionNoWidening`.
- [ ] Given user B's portal session, GET and approve on user A's grant both return 404 with the same bytes as an unknown id and A's grant stays pending.
- [ ] Given an approve POST without X-Warden-CSRF or with a foreign Origin, the response is 403 {"error":"csrf"} and nothing changes; a console session cookie alone gets 401.
- [ ] Given a purpose containing `<script>` and a URL, the rendered page contains them only as text under the 'not verified' label (DOM test in grants_test.go).

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-02`](delegation-grants.md#212--w-p4-dgr-02) Add the agent grant request API; [`W-P3-CSIG-04`](consent-auth.md#47--w-p3-csig-04) Add the portal session middleware, CSRF, logout and console isolation; [`W-P3-PORT-01`](consent-portal.md#17--w-p3-port-01) Serve the portal page and the connections list API

### 4/12 · W-P4-DGR-04

**Add the grant subject resolver, delegation mode and rollout guard to the token service**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#170](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/170)

Register a tokensvc SubjectResolver for `urn:warden:params:token-type:grant` so an agent can exchange an approved grant for a short-lived, grant-bound Warden token without a fresh ID token. Add the admin-only `agents[].delegation` setting so an agent can be forced to use grants, and refuse grant exchange while a worker serving the agent cannot enforce grants. CP-only; non-grant tokens stay byte-identical.

**Requirements**

- New internal/tokensvc/subject_grant.go: grantResolver registered in the W-P2-TOKX-02 resolver map only when grants are enabled; Exchange is not rewritten. subject_token is the grant id; the resolver reads it through a narrow tokensvc.GrantSource interface on every exchange (no cache).
- Checks: the grant exists and agent_id equals the assertion agent (else invalid_grant/grant_not_found externally, recorded as grant_agent_mismatch for a mismatch); pending, denied, revoked, expired or expires_at <= now map to grant_pending|grant_denied|grant_revoked|grant_expired; an idp_links row with link_state offboarded gives user_offboarded; a store error gives temporarily_unavailable/grant_store_unavailable. The common steps then run on the snapshot subject: agent active, BlockChecker, groups snapshot against current allowed_groups, scope.
- Minting: header typ `wgt+jwt`; sub, idp_iss, email, groups from the snapshot; act.sub = agent; sid from SessionStore.Touch(iss, sub, agent) so session revoke and offboarding apply; cnf.jkt from the assertion key; extra claims grant_id, tools (sorted) and providers (sorted) added to identity.WardenClaims with omitempty; exp = min(iat+ttl, grant expires_at). Over 12 KiB gives token_too_large.
- Delegation mode: new `agents[].delegation: optional|required` (default optional) in SettingsWire with DeepCopy and round-trip support, admin-only in the W-P1-SSO-05 per-field settings check. When required, id_token exchange for that agent gives invalid_grant/grant_required.
- Rollout guard: grant exchange gives temporarily_unavailable/grant_unenforceable while any connected worker reporting that agentID lacks heartbeat cap `grants/v1`, using the per-worker agentID and caps stored by W-P2-AREG-03 and W-P1-BLOCK-04; the settings save that enables grants or delegation required returns 409 workers_lack_capability unless an admin passes force=true (audited), as in W-P2-WBND-07.
- Add grant_not_found, grant_pending, grant_denied, grant_revoked, grant_expired, grant_agent_mismatch, grant_required, grant_unenforceable, grant_store_unavailable and user_offboarded to the closed Reason enum, docs/token-service.md and the p2-security-tests pin. cpstate migration tokensvc/0004 adds grant_id to token_events; the warden.token.v1 line gains grant_id. Tools and purpose are never logged.
- An optional GrantBlockedHook(grant_id, reason) is called on grant_revoked and grant_expired denials for W-P4-DGR-09 and never blocks the response. Exchange p99 stays at or under 25ms with one extra indexed read.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/tokensvc/subject_grant.go with grantResolver and the GrantSource interface; adapter in new internal/controlplane/grantsource.go over grants.Store and the idp_links LinkStore (tokensvc never imports grants or controlplane).
2. internal/identity/wardenclaims.go: add GrantID, Tools and Providers with omitempty and a typ selector so grant tokens use `wgt+jwt`.
3. internal/tokensvc reasons file: add the new reasons; update docs/token-service.md and the pinned list in the security tests.
4. internal/config: add AgentSettings.Delegation with validation, DeepCopy and SettingsWire round-trip; mark it admin-only in the per-field settings check.
5. internal/tokensvc exchange path: refuse id_token exchange for delegation-required agents; add the grants/v1 capability guard through a WorkerCaps interface wired from the worker registry.
6. cpstate migration tokensvc/0004 and the token_events writer carry grant_id.
7. Tests in new internal/tokensvc/subject_grant_test.go: TestGrantExchangeClaims (golden), TestGrantExchangeStates (table), TestGrantTokenExpNeverExceedsGrant, TestGrantBlockedUserRefused, TestDelegationRequiredRefusesIDToken, TestGrantRefusedWhileWorkerLacksCap, TestNonGrantTokensUnchanged (golden).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an active grant for agent A with tools [a,b], A's exchange returns a token with typ wgt+jwt, grant_id, tools [a,b], sub = user, act.sub = A and exp-iat <= 900: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestGrantExchangeClaims`.
- [ ] Given grants in pending, denied, revoked and expired status and one active but past expires_at, each returns 400 invalid_grant with the matching description and no issuance row: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestGrantExchangeStates`.
- [ ] Given agent B presenting agent A's grant id, the response equals the unknown-id response and token_events records grant_agent_mismatch.
- [ ] Given `delegation: required` for agent A, A's id_token exchange returns invalid_grant/grant_required; given a connected worker for A without grants/v1, A's grant exchange returns temporarily_unavailable/grant_unenforceable.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run 'TestMetricReasonsBounded|TestNonGrantTokensUnchanged'` passes, showing the enum is pinned and id_token tokens are byte-identical to the W-P2-TOKX-02 golden.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-01`](delegation-grants.md#112--w-p4-dgr-01) Add grants config, model, SQLite store and transitions; [`W-P2-TOKX-04`](token-exchange.md#47--w-p2-tokx-04) Add rate limits, issuance records and metrics for token exchange; [`W-P2-WBND-07`](identity-enforcement.md#710--w-p2-wbnd-07) Refuse require mode for agents served by workers without the capability

### 5/12 · W-P4-DGR-05

**Enforce grant tools in worker MCP verdicts**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#171](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/171)

Teach the worker to verify grant tokens and narrow MCP tools/call to the grant's tool set on every transport that sees a verified identity. The check reuses the W-P1-GPOL-04 `gateway.RequestMeta{Subject}` seam instead of adding a second OnRequest variant, and it cannot be switched off by MCP mode, a disabled gateway or an unparseable body. Worker-only; events without a grant stay byte-identical.

**Requirements**

- internal/identity: the WardenVerifier accepts typ `wgt+jwt` and parses grant_id, tools and providers into identity.Claims once per verify (cached with the result LRU entry); tools over 64 entries or outside the DGR-01 grammar give invalid/malformed. SubjectFrom fills Subject.GrantID, GrantTools (immutable set) and GrantProviders.
- internal/mcp/gateway: when meta.Subject has a GrantID, after the policy, AllowWhen and task-scope checks (around the existing mcp_out_of_scope block in OnRequest), a tool not in GrantTools adds a high-severity Finding `mcp_grant_scope` and the verdict is Deny whatever mcp.mode is. Matching: bare entries match the bare name; `server__tool` matches only when the server id is known from the registry host mapping, otherwise no match. Policy reasons stay dominant when both deny. Known behaviour, accepted for P4: the check runs after ToolPolicy.Evaluate, so an out-of-grant call that policy allows consumes one tool rate-limit token before the grant denies it; no non-consuming evaluate is added.
- With a GrantID, a body that ParseToolCall cannot read (including JSON-RPC batch arrays) is denied with `mcp_grant_unparsed` whatever FailClosedOnError says. A worker whose MCP gateway is nil or disabled answers requests carrying a grant token with 403 `grant_unenforceable`. stdio (`warden mcp`) carries no token and is documented as out of scope.
- Delegation mode: an MCP tools/call from a Warden token without grant_id for an agent with served `delegation: required` is denied with `mcp_grant_required`.
- Covers internal/proxy/http.go mcpRequestScan (HTTP/1 and h2) and the WebSocket pump (internal/mcp/ws/pump.go), which already pass the verified subject through RequestMeta after W-P1-GPOL-04.
- Recording: analytics.Event.GrantID (json grant_id, omitempty) with local SQLite addColumnIfAbsent in insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs; auditlog.FromEvent and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json gain grant_id with a schema_rev bump; mcp_grant_scope, mcp_grant_unparsed, mcp_grant_required and grant_unenforceable join internal/proxy/reasons.go. Tool names and grant ids never become metric labels.
- RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds cap `grants/v1`. The grant check is a map lookup with 0 allocs/op on the allowed path.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/identity/warden.go and claims: accept `wgt+jwt`, parse and validate grant claims, extend Subject with GrantID, GrantTools and GrantProviders.
2. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go: add grantCheck(meta, call) after the task-scope block in OnRequest; force Deny for grant findings regardless of applyMode; make failVerdict deny with mcp_grant_unparsed when meta carries a GrantID.
3. internal/proxy/http.go: before mcpRequestScan, refuse grant tokens with 403 grant_unenforceable when s.gw is nil or disabled; apply the delegation-required check from served agent settings.
4. internal/analytics/analytics.go, internal/auditlog and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json: add grant_id and bump schema_rev; stamp it where W-P1-VRFY-03 stamps user fields.
5. internal/proxy/reasons.go: add the new reasons; internal/config/remote.go Heartbeat: add `grants/v1`.
6. Tests: gateway TestGrantScopeNarrows, TestGrantNeverWidens, TestGrantNamespacedEntryFailsClosed, TestGrantMonitorModeStillDenies, TestGrantBatchBodyDenied, TestGrantDenyConsumesRateToken; proxy TestGrantScopeAllTransports, TestGrantUnenforceableWhenMCPOff; BenchmarkGrantCheck.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given base policy allow [a,b] and a grant token with tools [a], tools/call b in enforce mode gets 403 with Event.Reason=mcp_grant_scope and Event.GrantID set: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestGrantScopeNarrows`.
- [ ] Given a grant with tools [a,x] where x is denied by policy, x is denied with mcp_tool_denied and a is allowed: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestGrantNeverWidens`.
- [ ] Given mcp.mode monitor, tools/call b with a grant for [a] is still denied with mcp_grant_scope; with MCP disabled the request gets 403 grant_unenforceable; a batch array body gets mcp_grant_unparsed: `go test ./internal/proxy -run 'TestGrantUnenforceableWhenMCPOff|TestGrantMonitorModeStillDenies'`.
- [ ] Given the same grant over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and a WebSocket MCP session, tools/call b is denied on all three: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGrantScopeAllTransports`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestSchemaMatchesRecord` passes with grant_id mapped, and `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkGrantCheck -benchmem` reports 0 allocs/op.
- [ ] Given tool b with rate limit 2/min allowed by policy and a grant for [a], one denied tools/call b followed by two allowed calls to b from a token without a grant leaves the second of those denied with the rate-limit reason, pinning the accepted known behaviour: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestGrantDenyConsumesRateToken`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-04`](delegation-grants.md#412--w-p4-dgr-04) Add the grant subject resolver, delegation mode and rollout guard to the token service; [`W-P1-GPOL-04`](identity-policy.md#49--w-p1-gpol-04) Support groups/users in MCP tool allowWhen conditions; [`W-P2-WBND-03`](identity-enforcement.md#310--w-p2-wbnd-03) Enforce identity require mode on CONNECT and terminated traffic; [`W-P1-JAUD-02`](audit-log-export.md#46--w-p1-jaud-02) Publish decision v1 JSON Schema with closed-field and leak tests; [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#39--w-p1-vrfy-03) Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync

### 6/12 · W-P4-DGR-06

**Add grant revocation routes, revokedGrants bundle section and offboard step**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#172](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/172)

Give owners, admins and offboarding a way to revoke grants, and publish revoked grant ids to workers as a named signed-bundle section. The token service already refuses revoked grants on the next exchange because it reads the store each time; the section makes live tokens die on workers within one long-poll. Owner and admin routes stay on separate portal and console stacks, as W-P3-CSIG-04 requires. CP-only; the worker side is W-P4-DGR-10.

**Requirements**

- `POST /portal/api/grants/{id}/revoke` (owner only, portal session, X-Warden-CSRF, 404 for others) and `POST /dashboard/api/grants/{id}/revoke` plus bulk `POST /dashboard/api/grants/revoke` {sub|agent} (admin role; authz rows Action grant.revoke, Target grants, Scope `grants:write`, Audited true; optional reason_class from a closed set). All call one grants.Service.Revoke; an already revoked grant returns 200 with its terminal state.
- Revocation works from pending and active. Owner and admin revokes write adminaudit rows; offboarding and agent cancels write grant_events rows. Responses are 200 {status: revoked, workers_without_cap:[...]} listing connected workers for the agent that lack `grants/v1`.
- internal/bundle registers section `revokedGrants` = [{id, until}] sorted by id, with until = revoked_at + tokenService.ttl + identity clockSkewSeconds. policyServer.Refresh builds it from grants.Store, so it survives restarts; entries past until are dropped; with no entries the key is absent and the bundle is byte-identical.
- Each revoke appends a policy_publish_log row with new reason `grant_revoked`, calls Refresh and wakes long-poll waiters; revokes within 1s are coalesced into one row. Above 10,000 entries the CP keeps the previous envelope, logs at error and raises a Finding.
- Offboarding: append a `revoke_delegation_grants` Step to the W-P3-OFFB-01 contain list through a narrow offboard.GrantRevoker{RevokeAllForUser(ctx, iss, sub, actor)} interface wired by controlplane; internal/offboard never imports internal/grants and Offboard itself is not edited.
- Revoke buttons with a confirm dialog on /portal/grants and in the console. Logs `msg=grant_revoked grant_prefix by_kind` with no email.
- Register new API key scope `grants:write` (admin) with the W-P2-APIK-01 scope registry; the admin revoke rows use it, so a key never revokes on a viewer or editor owner's behalf.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/grants/service.go: Service.Revoke and RevokeBulk(by sub or agent), recording through grants.Recorder and calling a RevocationPublisher seam.
2. New internal/portal/grants_revoke.go (owner route) and new internal/dashboard/grants.go admin revoke handlers behind a new dashboard.GrantSource seam; add the authz rows.
3. internal/bundle: register the `revokedGrants` section; internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: build it in Refresh, add publish_log reason `grant_revoked` and a 1s coalescing timer.
4. internal/offboard: append the revoke_delegation_grants Step; adapter in internal/controlplane/offboard.go.
5. Tests: TestGrantRevokeAuthz, TestRevokedGrantsSection (byte-identical when empty), TestRevokedGrantsPruned, TestRevokeCoalesced, TestExchangeRefusesRevokedImmediately, TestOffboard_RevokesGrants.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given user B's portal session or a console editor, revoking A's grant returns 404 and 403 respectively and the grant is unchanged; the owner and an admin succeed: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestGrantRevokeAuthz`.
- [ ] Given a revoke, the next signed bundle carries the grant id in revokedGrants and a publish_log row with reason grant_revoked: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestRevokedGrantsSection`.
- [ ] Given the fake clock past revoked_at + ttl + skew, the next Refresh omits the id, and a bundle with no entries has no revokedGrants key.
- [ ] Given a revoked grant, the next token exchange for it returns invalid_grant/grant_revoked.
- [ ] Given an offboard run for a user with one active and one pending grant, both end revoked with revoked_by_kind offboard: `go test ./internal/offboard -run TestOffboard_RevokesGrants`.

### 7/12 · W-P4-DGR-07

**Add the grant expiry sweeper, console list, fleet column and CP metrics**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#173](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/173)

Expire pending and active grants on time, give admins a console view of every grant, and carry grant_id into the CP fleet store so traffic can be filtered by grant. Lifecycle audit rows are written by the tickets that make each transition; this ticket adds only the system expiry rows. CP-only, and the fleet column is split from the worker change in W-P4-DGR-05 per the lane convention.

**Requirements**

- New grants.Sweeper started from Server.Start when grants are enabled: interval grants.sweepInterval (default 1m, minimum 10s), calls ExpireDue, writes one grant_events `expired` row (actor system:grants) per flipped grant and stops on context cancel; a sweep error is logged and retried on the next tick. It is idempotent and single-replica until P5.
- `GET /dashboard/api/grants?user=&agent=&status=&cursor=&limit=` (viewer role; Scope `grants:read`; limit default 50, max 200; 400 on a malformed parameter) through the dashboard.GrantSource seam; never returns purpose text longer than the stored cap or any token.
- Console Grants tab in internal/dashboard/index.html: list with filters, every field rendered with textContent, Revoke and bulk revoke shown only to admins and calling the W-P4-DGR-06 routes through the api() wrapper; hidden when grants are disabled.
- FleetSQLiteStore adds grant_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' via addColumnIfAbsent and an index (grant_id, ts), carried through StoreAggregatedEvent, GetEvents and GetAggregatedEvents, and /dashboard/api/traffic accepts ?grant=.
- In-memory counters warden_cp_grants_transitions_total{to} and gauge warden_cp_grants{status}, nil-safe and ready for W-P5-RETN-06 export; no user, agent or grant id labels.
- Register new API key scope `grants:read` (viewer) with the W-P2-APIK-01 scope registry for the list route; TestAuthzRouteCoverage passes with both grant rows classified.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/grants/sweeper.go: Sweeper.Run(ctx) with an injectable clock; start it in internal/controlplane Server.Start.
2. internal/dashboard/grants.go: list handler with filter parsing and cursor paging; authz row.
3. internal/dashboard/index.html: Grants tab, filters and admin revoke controls.
4. internal/analytics fleet store: grant_id column, index and query plumbing; traffic filter.
5. internal/grants/metrics.go: transitions counter and status gauge.
6. Tests: TestExpirySweeper, TestSweeperOneEventPerTransition, TestGrantsListFilters, TestGrantsTabHiddenWhenDisabled, TestFleetGrantIDMigration.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an active grant expiring at T and sweepInterval 1m on a fake clock, at T+61s it is expired with exactly one grant_events expired row, even after further sweeps: `go test ./internal/grants -run TestExpirySweeper`.
- [ ] Given grants for two users, two agents and three statuses, GET /dashboard/api/grants filters each dimension, pages with nextCursor and returns 400 for status=bogus: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestGrantsListFilters`.
- [ ] Given an old fleet DB opened twice, the grant_id column is added once with no data loss: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestFleetGrantIDMigration`.
- [ ] Given a viewer session, the Grants tab lists grants but shows no revoke control, and an editor's direct POST to the revoke route gets 403.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-01`](delegation-grants.md#112--w-p4-dgr-01) Add grants config, model, SQLite store and transitions; [`W-P4-DGR-06`](delegation-grants.md#612--w-p4-dgr-06) Add grant revocation routes, revokedGrants bundle section and offboard step

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-DGR-12`](delegation-grants.md#1212--w-p4-dgr-12) Document delegation grants and test the done-when end to end

### 8/12 · W-P4-DGR-08

**Add grant status long-poll, renew and cancel endpoints**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#174](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/174)

Let the agent wait for the user's decision, renew a grant that is about to expire, and give up a grant it no longer needs. Status uses POST with a form body because the agent's client assertion cannot travel in a GET query string without leaking into access logs. Renew is limited so an agent cannot re-prompt a user who just denied or revoked it. CP-only.

**Requirements**

- `POST /oauth2/grants/{id}/status` (form: client_assertion_type, client_assertion, wait, optional since_status), verified with VerifyClientAssertion and the ReplayStore. wait uses longpoll.ParseWait (W-P3-JIT-04, 1s-60s; absent answers at once). Response 200 {id, status, expires_at, pending_expires_at, tools, providers} with Cache-Control: no-store and no sub, email or purpose.
- The handler returns at once when the status differs from since_status; otherwise it waits on grants.Store.Subscribe(id), re-reads on wake, every 5s and at the deadline, and caps waiters at 8 per grant and 1,024 in total (429 rate_limited with Retry-After: 1). A client disconnect frees its waiter at once.
- `POST /oauth2/grants/{id}/renew` is allowed from active grants within grants.expiryNoticeBefore of expiry and from expired grants. It creates a new pending grant with renewed_from, copying agent, identity snapshot, purpose, tools and providers, re-validated against current policy (removed entries dropped and reported as dropped) and re-clamped by maxTTL, and counts against the pending caps. Denied and revoked grants give 409 grant_not_renewable; the agent must send a new POST /oauth2/grants with a fresh ID token.
- `POST /oauth2/grants/{id}/cancel` moves the agent's own pending or active grant to revoked with revoked_by_kind agent and publishes like any revoke.
- Another agent's or an unknown grant returns the same 404 body on all three routes. Each route has an authz row classified assertion-authenticated, ScopeNone, Audited:false; renew and cancel write grant_events rows and renew calls the nil-safe Notifier with grant_approval.
- Gauge warden_cp_grant_status_waiters; debug-level log `msg=grant_status_poll agent grant_prefix waited_ms outcome`; no assertion or jti in logs.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/controlplane/grants_http.go: handleGrantStatus using longpoll.ParseWait and Store.Subscribe, with the waiter counters.
2. internal/grants/service.go: Renew and Cancel with the renewability rules and re-validation shared with Request.
3. Mount handleGrantRenew and handleGrantCancel; cancel calls Service.Revoke so the W-P4-DGR-06 publisher runs.
4. Add the authz rows and extend TestAuthzRouteCoverage.
5. Tests: TestGrantStatusLongPoll, TestGrantStatusReplayRejected, TestGrantRenew, TestGrantRenewDenied409, TestGrantCancel, TestGrantOtherAgent404, TestGrantStatusWaiterCap.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a waiter with wait=30s on a pending grant, when the owner approves at t=2s the waiter returns active within 1s; with no change it returns pending at 30s on the fake clock: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestGrantStatusLongPoll`.
- [ ] Given an expired grant, renew creates a new pending grant with renewed_from set and the old grant unchanged; a denied or revoked grant returns 409 grant_not_renewable: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestGrantRenew`.
- [ ] Given agent B's valid assertion, status, renew and cancel on agent A's grant return the same 404 body as an unknown id.
- [ ] Given the same assertion reused for a second poll, the response is 401 invalid_client (replay).
- [ ] Given 9 concurrent waiters on one grant, the 9th gets 429 with Retry-After.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-02`](delegation-grants.md#212--w-p4-dgr-02) Add the agent grant request API; [`W-P4-DGR-06`](delegation-grants.md#612--w-p4-dgr-06) Add grant revocation routes, revokedGrants bundle section and offboard step; [`W-P3-JIT-04`](jit-authorization.md#47--w-p3-jit-04) Add /connect/{id}/status long-poll on the CP

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-DGR-12`](delegation-grants.md#1212--w-p4-dgr-12) Document delegation grants and test the done-when end to end

### 9/12 · W-P4-DGR-09

**Send grant approval, expiring and blocked notifications**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#175](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/175)

Wire the grants.Notifier seam to internal/notify so users hear about new grant requests, grants about to expire and agents blocked by a revoked or expired grant. Dedupe is stored in cpstate so a CP restart does not resend. Payloads carry only Warden-built fields and a portal link. CP-only.

**Requirements**

- Adapter from grants.Notifier to notify.Service.Send (wired by W-P4-NTFY-08) in internal/controlplane, always with Ref `grant:<id>` so the notify dedup families apply; `grant_approval` on create and renew carries the registry display name, tool count, expiry and the approve_url, never the purpose.
- Expiry notices: a sweep on grants.noticeInterval (default 1h) sends `grant_expiring` for active grants whose remaining time is below min(grants.expiryNoticeBefore, lifetime/4) and expiry_notified_at is null, then sets expiry_notified_at, so a crash re-sends at most once.
- `grant_blocked`: the W-P4-DGR-04 GrantBlockedHook enqueues a send on grant_revoked or grant_expired exchange denials; cpstate migration `grants/0002` adds grant_notices(grant_id, kind, last_sent_at, PRIMARY KEY(grant_id, kind)) as a cheap pre-filter: a send is enqueued only when last_sent_at is older than 24h, matching the notify grant_blocked family window (W-P4-NTFY-04), so a hammering agent does not write outbox rows and both checks agree across restarts. The hook never blocks the token response.
- Payloads contain only the display name, an 8-character grant id prefix, counts, expires_at and the action link consent.publicURL/portal/grants/<id>, which notify builds itself (callers never pass a URL); never a token, assertion, purpose or tool arguments.
- When notify is not configured the adapter is nil, the notice sweep does not start and the hook is a no-op, logged once at INFO. Counter warden_cp_grant_notices_total{kind,outcome} has no per-user labels.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/controlplane/grant_notify.go: notify adapter implementing grants.Notifier and the GrantBlockedHook.
2. New internal/grants/notices.go: the expiry notice sweep and the grant_notices dedupe store with migration grants/0002.
3. Wire both in Server.Start only when notify and grants are enabled.
4. Tests: TestApprovalNotificationSent, TestExpiryNoticeOnce, TestBlockedNoticeDedup, TestNoticeNoLeak (canary strings), TestNoNotifyNoSweeper.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an active grant expiring in 71h and 30 hourly sweeps on a fake clock, exactly one grant_expiring send is recorded: `go test ./internal/grants -run TestExpiryNoticeOnce`.
- [ ] Given 50 grant_revoked denials for one grant in a day with a CP restart between them, exactly one grant_blocked send is recorded, and one more is allowed 24h after the first: `go test ./internal/grants -run TestBlockedNoticeDedup`.
- [ ] Given canary strings for a minted token, the assertion and the purpose, none appear in any captured payload, log line or audit row: `go test ./internal/grants -run TestNoticeNoLeak`.
- [ ] Given notify not configured, a revoked-grant exchange still returns invalid_grant within the W-P2-TOKX-02 latency budget and no notice sweeper runs.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-02`](delegation-grants.md#212--w-p4-dgr-02) Add the agent grant request API; [`W-P4-DGR-04`](delegation-grants.md#412--w-p4-dgr-04) Add the grant subject resolver, delegation mode and rollout guard to the token service; [`W-P4-NTFY-08`](user-notify.md#810--w-p4-ntfy-08) Add CP-local notifications config block and CP wiring

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-DGR-12`](delegation-grants.md#1212--w-p4-dgr-12) Document delegation grants and test the done-when end to end

### 10/12 · W-P4-DGR-10

**Apply revokedGrants on workers and close revoked grant sessions**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#313](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/313)

Make a revoked grant's live token stop working on every pinned worker within one bundle long-poll. The worker reads the `revokedGrants` section from the verified bundle, rejects tokens whose grant_id is listed, and closes sessions that were opened with them. Worker-only, split from W-P4-DGR-06.

**Requirements**

- On each verified bundle apply, the `revokedGrants` section from RemoteProvider.Bundle() is swapped atomically into the identity snapshot as a set; a bundle without the section yields an empty set.
- A Warden token whose grant_id is in the set gets status invalid with new reason `grant_revoked` (added to the W-P2-WBND-04 reason set and identity metrics); the check runs on every verify and on every terminated MCP request, and the snapshot generation change invalidates cached results.
- In every identity mode, an MCP tools/call carrying a verified token whose grant_id is revoked is denied with `mcp_grant_revoked`; it is never downgraded to anonymous traffic.
- After each apply, sessions registered in the W-P1-BLOCK-05 registry whose grant_id was newly revoked are closed through the W-P2-WBND-09 post-apply re-check, each writing one deny event with Reason grant_revoked and calling RecordBlocked.
- No revoked id list is logged; logs carry counts and 8-character prefixes only.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/identity: add the revoked-grant set to the WardenVerifier snapshot and the grant_revoked reason.
2. internal/worker/applier.go: read `revokedGrants` from the verified bundle and pass it with the token keys on apply.
3. internal/proxy: register grant_id with sessions in the W-P1-BLOCK-05 registry and add CloseRevokedGrantSessions to the post-apply hook; add mcp_grant_revoked and grant_revoked to reasons.go.
4. Tests: TestRevokedGrantRejected, TestRevokedGrantDeniedAfterBundleApply, TestRevokedGrantNotAnonymousInAttributeMode, TestRevokedGrantSessionClosed.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a live grant token accepted by a require-mode worker, after a bundle listing its grant_id is applied the next request is denied with grant_revoked: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestRevokedGrantRejected`.
- [ ] Given an open raw tunnel and a WebSocket session opened with that token, both are closed after the apply with one deny event each: `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestRevokedGrantSessionClosed`.
- [ ] Given attribute mode, tools/call with the revoked token is denied with mcp_grant_revoked and not treated as anonymous: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestRevokedGrantNotAnonymousInAttributeMode`.
- [ ] Given a bundle without revokedGrants, the revoked set is empty and existing tokens verify as before.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-05`](delegation-grants.md#512--w-p4-dgr-05) Enforce grant tools in worker MCP verdicts; [`W-P4-DGR-06`](delegation-grants.md#612--w-p4-dgr-06) Add grant revocation routes, revokedGrants bundle section and offboard step; [`W-P2-WBND-09`](identity-enforcement.md#910--w-p2-wbnd-09) Close require-mode sessions at token expiry and document require mode; [`W-P2-SBND-04`](signed-bundles.md#47--w-p2-sbnd-04) Verify signed bundles in RemoteProvider and keep last-known-good in memory

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-DGR-12`](delegation-grants.md#1212--w-p4-dgr-12) Document delegation grants and test the done-when end to end

### 11/12 · W-P4-DGR-11

**Limit per-user secret swaps to the grant's providers**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#314](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/314)

A grant names the per-user providers the agent may use, so a grant for 'read calendar' must not let the agent's traffic pick up the user's GitHub token. Under a grant token the worker's W-P3-PUS-09 UserTokenSource path swaps a per-user credential only for providers in the `providers` claim. Worker-only.

**Requirements**

- When the verified subject carries a GrantID, a per-user secret swap for provider p happens only when p is in Subject.GrantProviders; an empty or absent list allows no per-user providers.
- Any other per-user swap is refused before the UserTokenSource is called: 403 JSON {"error":"grant_provider_scope"} on terminated HTTP and an MCPError via the internal/connect builder on MCP, with Event.Reason grant_provider_scope and no upstream request.
- Tokens without grant_id keep the existing W-P3-PUS-09 behaviour byte for byte.
- grant_provider_scope joins internal/proxy/reasons.go and the decision schema reason list; Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10) is not set for a refused swap. No provider token or mapping value is logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/proxy per-user swap path (where W-P3-PUS-09 calls UserTokenSource.AccessToken): add the grant provider check before the call.
2. Build the 403 and MCP error responses with the existing builders; add the reason to internal/proxy/reasons.go and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json.
3. Tests: TestGrantProviderSwapAllowed, TestGrantProviderSwapRefused, TestNonGrantSwapUnchanged.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a grant token with providers [google] and per-user mappings for google and github, a request to the github host gets 403 grant_provider_scope and the fake UserTokenSource is not called: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGrantProviderSwapRefused`.
- [ ] Given the same token, a request to the google host gets the swapped credential and Event.UserTokenProvider=google.
- [ ] Given a token without grant_id, both swaps behave as before: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestNonGrantSwapUnchanged`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-05`](delegation-grants.md#512--w-p4-dgr-05) Enforce grant tools in worker MCP verdicts; [`W-P3-PUS-09`](refresh-model.md#912--w-p3-pus-09) Add the worker UserTokenSource with memory cache and epoch invalidation; [`W-P3-PUS-10`](refresh-model.md#1012--w-p3-pus-10) Record the per-user token provider on analytics events

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-DGR-12`](delegation-grants.md#1212--w-p4-dgr-12) Document delegation grants and test the done-when end to end

### 12/12 · W-P4-DGR-12

**Document delegation grants and test the done-when end to end**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#315](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/315)

Harness authors need the request, approve, poll, exchange and error contract, and operators need the rollout, require-mode caveat, revocation timing and restore runbook. Add docs/delegation-grants.md and one integration test that runs the feature's done_when against an in-process CP, OIDC issuer and worker. Test and docs only.

**Requirements**

- New docs/delegation-grants.md: the agent contract for POST /oauth2/grants, /status, /renew and /cancel (all under `/oauth2/grants*` with the /oauth2/token client-assertion auth) and the grant token exchange, with request and response examples and every status code and reason; the token claims (typ wgt+jwt, grant_id, tools, providers).
- Operator section: the `grants:` block, its defaults (maxTTL 168h with a 2160h hard cap, pendingTTL 24h, maxTools 32 with a 64 hard cap, purpose 200 runes) and startup checks, the known behaviour that an out-of-grant call allowed by policy still consumes one tool rate-limit token, `agents[].delegation`, the `grants/v1` rollout order (upgrade every worker first), the guarantee only for identity require plus delegation required, revocation timing (immediate at the token service, one bundle long-poll at workers, at most one TTL with the CP down), degraded modes and the post-restore bulk revoke runbook.
- docs/control-plane.md and docs/token-service.md link to the new page and list the new routes, reasons and config keys.
- Integration test (build tag integration, in-process OIDC issuer, CP and worker): request, portal approve with narrowing, exchange, MCP call inside and outside the grant over HTTP and WebSocket, id_token exchange refused under delegation required, revoke, deny and session close after the next bundle apply, and CP restart with state intact.
- The test asserts no token, assertion or purpose canary appears in captured logs, events or audit rows.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write docs/delegation-grants.md and update docs/control-plane.md, docs/token-service.md and docs/architecture.md links.
2. New test/integration/grants_test.go using the existing integration harness helpers for CP, worker and OIDC issuer.
3. Add a canary log capture helper check shared with earlier security tests.
4. Run the suite in CI under the integration tag.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestDelegationGrantsEndToEnd` passes and covers every clause of the feature done_when.
- [ ] After revoke, the worker denies the grant token and closes its WebSocket session within one long-poll in the test (under 2s).
- [ ] No canary string for tokens, assertions or purpose appears in any captured output.
- [ ] `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` passes and docs/delegation-grants.md lists every reason added by this feature.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-DGR-07`](delegation-grants.md#712--w-p4-dgr-07) Add the grant expiry sweeper, console list, fleet column and CP metrics; [`W-P4-DGR-08`](delegation-grants.md#812--w-p4-dgr-08) Add grant status long-poll, renew and cancel endpoints; [`W-P4-DGR-09`](delegation-grants.md#912--w-p4-dgr-09) Send grant approval, expiring and blocked notifications; [`W-P4-DGR-10`](delegation-grants.md#1012--w-p4-dgr-10) Apply revokedGrants on workers and close revoked grant sessions; [`W-P4-DGR-11`](delegation-grants.md#1112--w-p4-dgr-11) Limit per-user secret swaps to the grant's providers
